Subject: Post-call: model fit & prompt collection — ACME (next steps)

Hi Jordan / Priya,

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation and great context on the search & summarization workflows you're looking to enable. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay synced: 

Recap
- Primary product flows: customer support article summarization + search ranking + automated response suggestions.
- Volume/latency targets: ~200 reqs/min on peak; target 200–800ms p95 for short responses, longer for full-doc summarization.
- Data sensitivity: some prompts will contain customer-reported PII (emails, order numbers) and internal notes.

Next steps (action items)
1) ACME: please share a sample prompt set (10–20 representative prompts) across happy-path, edge cases, and failure modes. Mark any PHI/PII. Use the attached prompt_collection_template.csv if helpful.
2) ACME: flag any redaction rules or examples where content must be removed before sending to an external model.
3) Redwood: we'll propose 2–3 model candidates with benchmark links, and a short plan for evals and monitoring (quality/regression checks).
4) Schedule: if we get prompts this week, we can run a first-pass eval + benchmark by next Wednesday.

Attachments: prompt_collection_template.csv (simple CSV with columns: prompt, expected_output, contains_pii, notes)

Questions for you: can you confirm which prompts are time-sensitive (need current data) vs static? Also any constraints around on-prem/VPC for this pilot?

Thanks — I’ll loop in Neha and Vivek for recommended benchmarks + redaction guidance once we have the sample prompts.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit & prompt collection — ACME (recommended models + eval plan)

Jordan / Priya,

Appreciate the sample prompts — very helpful. A few recommendations and clarifying items from our side: 

Recommended model candidates (first-pass)
- redwood-2-xl: best quality for long-form summarization and complex reasoning. Expect highest token cost but lower regression risk.
- redwood-2-small: cost-efficient for short responses and high-throughput search ranking. Good fallback for latency-critical routes.
- open-llama-3-7B-quant (int8): good cost/latency balance for non-sensitive summarization if you accept a modest drop in fidelity; watch for edge-case hallucinations.

Links & artifacts
- Benchmarks (internal report): benchmark_results_redwood_v1.pdf — covers p95 latency, perplexity, and task-specific F1 on our internal summarization suite.
- Evaluation harness (shared Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/ACME-prompt-collection — we'll drop the eval scripts and a small scoring harness there.
- HubSpot deal record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/ACME-12345

Quality & regression notes
- For quantized variants we typically see a small regression on extractive fidelity and entity preservation; to mitigate we recommend a lightweight eval suite that checks entity recall on a red-team prompt set.
- If you have PHI/PII, best practice is to redact before sending to hosted models. For Private/VPC deployments we can run evals inside your environment (we'll need a short onboarding checklist).

Ask for ACME
- Please tag each prompt row that contains PII/PHI and provide an example of how you'd like it redacted (e.g., replace email with [EMAIL_REDACTED], drop order ids, or pseudonymize).
- Add 3–5 explicit edge cases where you worry about hallucination or policy-sensitive outputs (e.g., contract language, billing disputes).

Plan & timeline
- If we have the annotated prompt set by EOD Fri (Aug 6), Redwood will run first-pass evals against redwood-2-xl and redwood-2-small and share a short report by Wed (Aug 12).

Attachments: redaction_guidance.docx, prompt_collection_template.csv (filled example)

One more thing — can you confirm the throughput latency SLO for the short responses (we want to pick batch sizes / kernels accordingly)?

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Quick reply — agree with the suggested thresholds. Couple specifics:
- Start with entity recall >= 0.85 on extractive tests; aim for 0.9 before recommending redwood-2-xl as primary.
- For hallucination, fail any output that invents an entity referenced in the source doc (we'll tag via exact-match checks); escalate if >5% of prompts fail on 100-sample run.
- Quantized variants: ok for non-sensitive routes, but require extra entity-preservation checks. Recommend flagging any prompt with high entity density to run on full-precision.

I'll take a look at redaction_guidance.docx and send comments by EOD.

-Neha
